title: Smyrna cross stitch
subtitle: An upright cross placed over a diagonal cross to form an eight-pointed shape
excerpt: Smyrna cross works a diagonal cross first, then an upright cross directly on top. The two crosses share the same four holes and together make an eight-pointed shape that stands noticeably above the canvas surface.
sourceNotes: Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Smyrna stitch entry. Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), canvaswork chapter.

glossaryTerms.definition: Two crosses worked on the same four canvas holes: first a diagonal cross stitch, then an upright cross placed on top. The combined stitch makes an eight-pointed shape.

heroPrompt: Smyrna cross stitches on 13-count canvas in deep red wool, showing rows of eight-pointed raised cross shapes, natural light.

content.text: Smyrna cross stitch places two crosses on the same four canvas holes. The first cross is diagonal: lower left to upper right, then lower right to upper left. The second cross is upright: bottom to top, then left to right. The upright cross sits on top of the diagonal, and the eight limbs give a prominent raised shape.
Work it in one colour for a bold textured repeat. Or use two colours: one for the diagonal cross, one for the upright, to show the star structure clearly.

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count mono canvas. A hoop or frame both work; a frame keeps the canvas squarer under the upright-cross tension

items.label: Thread
items.value: One strand of Persian wool. Two colours are optional but show the stitch structure clearly

content.text: Work a diagonal cross over a two-by-two canvas area: bring the needle up at the lower left, insert at the upper right. Bring the needle up at the lower right, insert at the upper left.
Now work the upright cross over the same four holes: bring the needle up at the bottom centre, insert at the top centre. Bring the needle up at the left centre, insert at the right centre.
The vertical stitch of the upright cross is the last stitch worked, and crosses the horizontal. Keep this consistent across the piece. Always the vertical on top.
Move two holes to the right for the next stitch. Work across the row.

items.cause: The four centre holes of the block do not align with the diagonal cross holes.
items.fix: On a two-by-two block, the centre holes are the same four holes as the diagonal cross corners. The mid-point of each side is where the upright cross arms enter and exit.

items.cause: Alternating which cross goes on top.
items.fix: Commit to vertical-on-top throughout the piece. Check every few stitches.
